prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a layered layout: the ceiling and foreground edges are nearest, the service counter spans the middle distance at roughly 1–3 m, and the back wall and equipment lie farther away at about 3–5 m. Across frames 1–3, a person remains directly ahead at approximately 1–2 m and becomes larger and brighter, while a near object or counter edge enters from the right within roughly 0.5–1 m; another person is partly cut off at the left edge in frame 1. In frames 4–5, the central person shifts toward the right and appears to turn side-on or move laterally, while a farther person becomes visible near the back counter at roughly 2–4 m; the foreground object on the right remains within the camera wearer’s arm-reach range. The map makes distance ordering, surface continuity, and near-edge occlusion clearer than RGB, but its absolute metre estimates are uncertain and bright halos around people, the ceiling, and image boundaries make thin limbs and reflective counter surfaces unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates people from the counter area and shows one main person ahead in frames 1–3, first about 1–2 m away and slightly left of centre, then centred and increasingly close; a second person is only partly visible at the far-left edge in frame 1 and another small person-shaped region appears behind or beside the main person in frame 2. In frame 3 the main person fills more of the foreground, with another person partly occluded immediately to their right, whereas frames 4–5 show a person farther right and more side-on, plus another person near the counter in frame 5; these people appear separated by roughly 1–3 m. The masks also identify large upper-wall regions as “tv” and small counter objects as a bottle and cup, locating the cup and bottle to the right of the frame-4 person and near that person’s reach, though these labels do not match the RGB reliably. Compared with RGB, the map clarifies instance boundaries and partial occlusions, but it misses most counter equipment and furniture, merges or truncates bodies, inconsistently detects people across frames, and appears to misclassify wall displays or openings as televisions.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides sparse orientation and articulation cues: in frames 1–3 the principal skeleton is directly ahead at about 1–2 m, with upper-body and arm keypoints indicating a mostly frontal or oblique orientation and an arm extending toward the image right in frames 2–3. The head keypoints face roughly toward the camera in the middle frames, but their low resolution does not establish gaze direction; the extended arm lies near another partly visible person or foreground region, while the exact separation and reach cannot be measured confidently. In frame 4 only a few upper-body points and one bent limb are recovered as the person shifts right and turns more side-on, and in frame 5 a larger right-side skeleton suggests a closer person, roughly 1–2 m away, with one arm angled leftward and much of the body incomplete. This map exposes limb configuration and turning that are harder to distinguish against the busy RGB background, but it supplies almost no scene layout or object distance, misses hands despite the expected hand channel, and contains disconnected or anatomically uncertain keypoints.
